items.title: Notice of Proposed Information Collection Requests: IMLS Grants to States Five-Year State Plan Guidelines for State Library Administrative Agencies for Fiscal Years 2028-2032
tags: National Foundation on the Arts and the Humanities
Institute of Museum and Library Services

agencies: National Foundation on the Arts and the Humanities
Institute of Museum and Library Services
data.abstract: The Institute of Museum and Library Services (IMLS), as part of its continuing effort to reduce paperwork and respondent burden, conducts a pre- clearance consultation program to provide the general public and Federal agencies with an opportunity to comment on proposed and/or continuing collections of information in accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA). The PRA ensures that data requested by the Federal Government can be provided in the desired format, reporting burden (time and financial resources) is minimized, collection instruments are clearly understood, and the impact of collection requirements on respondents can be properly assessed. This notice informs the public of the agency's intent to request renewal of the clearance for the IMLS Grants to States Five-Year State Plan Guidelines for State Library Administrative Agencies. The current five-year period covers fiscal years (FYs) 2022-2027. The upcoming five-year period will cover FYs 2028-2032, with Five-Year State Plans due to IMLS on June 30, 2027. A copy of the proposed information collection request can be obtained by contacting the individual listed below in the ADDRESSES section of this notice.

items.title: Northern States Power Company; Prairie Island Independent Spent Fuel Storage Installation; License Amendment Application

data.abstract: The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) has received a license amendment application from Northern States Power Company (NSPM) for an amendment to Materials License No. SNM-2506 for the Prairie Island Independent Spent Fuel Storage Installation (PI ISFSI) located in Welch, Minnesota. The amendment request seeks to change License Condition 26. The subject License Condition depends, in part, on the completion of the joint Electric Power Research Institute (EPRI) and Department of Energy (DOE) "High Burnup Dry Storage Cask Research and Development Project" (HDRP). License Condition 26 includes two requirements to provide evaluations to the NRC by specified due dates. Due to the change in the timeline for completing the evaluations from the HDRP initial period of storage, NSPM proposes to revise License Condition 26 to modify the due date of the first of these evaluations from April 4, 2028, to within six months of the HDRP initial storage period report publication date or April 4, 2033, whichever is earlier.

items.title: Change in Bank Control Notices; Acquisitions of Shares of a Bank or Bank Holding Company
Civil Penalties; Notice of Adjusted Maximum Amounts

data.abstract: In 1990, Congress enacted statutory amendments to adjust the maximum civil penalty amounts authorized under the Consumer Product Safety Act (CPSA), the Federal Hazardous Substances Act (FHSA), and the Flammable Fabrics Act (FFA). On August 14, 2008, the Consumer Product Safety Improvement Act of 2008 (CPSIA) increased the maximum civil penalty amounts to $100,000 for each violation and $15,000,000 for any related series of violations. The CPSIA tied the effective date of the new amounts to the earlier of the date on which final regulations are issued, or 1 year after August 14, 2008. The new amounts became effective on August 14, 2009. The CPSIA also revised the starting date, from December 1, 1994 to December 1, 2011, and December 1 of each fifth calendar year thereafter, on which the Commission must prescribe and publish in the Federal Register, the schedule of maximum authorized penalties. On December 1, 2021, the CPSC published increased maximum authorized civil penalty amounts of $120,000 for each violation and $17,150,000 for any related series of violations. As calculated in accordance with the amendments, the new amounts are $140,000 for each violation and $20,350,000 for any related series of violations.
